chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Abu Sa'id al-Adami narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Musa, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

He said: I was with him during the circumambulation (Tawaf). When we arrived at the Yemeni Corner, the Imam (peace be upon him) stood, raised his hand, and said: 'O God! O Master of well-being, O Provider of well-being, O Bestower of well-being, O Gracious in bestowing well-being, O Generous in granting well-being upon me and upon all Your creation, O Merciful of this world and the Hereafter, O Merciful of the Two Worlds! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and grant us well-being, the completion of well-being, and the perfection of well-being in the gratitude for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Most Merciful of the merciful.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yemeni Corner of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of the Yemeni Corner in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) recites this supplication at the Yemeni Corner, a site traditionally associated with the Prophet Ibrahim, emphasizing 'Al-Afiyah' (comprehensive well-being) not merely as physical health but as the spiritual capacity for gratitude. This practice highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating ritual worship with continuous thankfulness, linking the physical act of Tawaf with the spiritual state of recognizing divine favor.
